one-relation.arrow-frequency-are-one-bit.formal: With $C$ fixed, $J \mapsto -J$ forces $\gamma_{0} \mapsto -\gamma_{0}$, since $C(-J) = -(CJ)$; the rest rotation by $\pi$ about an axis in the spin plane flips $J$ while fixing $\gamma_{0}$, but it also flips $C$, so it is not a symmetry of the fixed law. Hence, given the law, the frequency sign, particle against antiparticle, and the direction of the frame's time are one bit and not two. This is the identification Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-flag-arrow-superselection} imports under Hypothesis (S), in this paper a one-line identity in $\Cl(1,3)$; it does not source the bit, which (S) still does, but it proves that the two readings of the bit cannot come apart, which the dark-matter paper asserts as ``spent once, read twice''.
one-relation.arrow-frequency-are-one-bit.technical:
Given the law $\nabla\psi = m\psi C$ with $C$ fixed, the imaginary unit $J$ and the rest-frame vector are tied by $\gamma_{0} = CJ$, so linearity gives $C(-J) = -(CJ)$: reversing the imaginary unit reverses the direction of the frame's time. The rest rotation by $\pi$ about an axis in the spin plane flips $J$ while fixing $\gamma_{0}$, but it also flips $C$, so it is not a symmetry of the fixed law.

Hence, given the law, the frequency sign (particle against antiparticle) and the direction of the frame's time are one bit, not two. This proves that the two readings of the bit cannot come apart; it does not source the bit, which still rests on Hypothesis (S) as the imported flag fact records.
one-relation.arrow-frequency-are-one-bit.lay: In the relativistic electron equation, the sign that separates particles from antiparticles and the direction in which a laboratory's time runs look like two separate choices. Once the form of the law is fixed, flipping one forces the other to flip, so they are a single yes-or-no choice. This does not explain where that choice comes from, which still rests on Hypothesis (S); it only shows that its two readings always agree.

Levels pass: lay now says the bit itself still rests on Hypothesis (S).

__notes__.note.one-relation.setting-introduction:
One relation carries both theories. The defining relation of a Clifford algebra, $\{e_{a}, e_{b}\} = 2g_{ab}\mathbf{1}$, reads on an orthogonal basis as a metric and on a Witt basis as the canonical anticommutation relations of a fermionic mode system. The metric \emph{is} the anticommutator and the anticommutator \emph{is} the metric: geometric versus quantum is a choice of chart on one object, not a choice of object. This paper develops that identification into a synthesis and then addresses its principal remaining task, the laboratory, deriving laboratory quantum mechanics as the slow shadow of the frozen phase (the series' name for the descended, condensed vacuum in which the laboratory is located) and carrying the account as far as the framework reaches, which is to the hard problem and no further.

The synthesis first. Witt index is quantum capacity, the tower paper's theorem \cite[Thm.~4.3]{ButlerT3}, and there are two of them: the real capacity $\min(p,q)$, the number of modes realisable by real null vectors, and the complex capacity $\lfloor (p+q)/2 \rfloor$ of the complexification. Lorentzian signature has real capacity one, so pre-ascent spacetime natively supports exactly one real quantum mode, the boost qubit; each ascent adjoins one hyperbolic plane, raising both capacities by one, so the transport principle \emph{is} capacity increment and the tower's one-qubit-per-rung ladder is its restatement, and the reading that Hawking thermality is single-mode because one rung was ascended is offered and labelled a reading; and the complexified ascended space has complex capacity three, the pair count under which the Standard-Model paper selects the strong force and four dimensions, on the conditionalities it declares. Every point of spacetime is null under the completion's embedding, so spacetime is a family of the algebra's non-invertible elements: division by zero is not confined to special loci but is the condition of every point. Each point's null vector acts on the twistor space as a nilpotent whose kernel is the point's incidence line, and every twistor on that line is the Fock vacuum of its own isotropic system: a point is not one vacuum but a projective line of them, and conformally compactified spacetime is the manifold of such lines, the Klein quadric, over which the two theories read as the dynamics \emph{of} the vacua (general relativity, how the vacuum family varies from point to point) and the dynamics \emph{above} a vacuum (quantum mechanics, excitations over a chosen vacuum). The series' internal cross-checks are then sorted by level: one count in two vocabularies, an identification, and a reading.

Then the laboratory, and there the paper is deliberately deflationary. Of the three postulated inputs of nonrelativistic quantum mechanics, one is sourced in structures derived before the question was asked, half of another is sourced under an open hypothesis and the other half is not, and the third was not a separate postulate: the mass is the condensate, at the level the families paper's reading holds; the time orientation that distinguishes particles from antiparticles is the planted flag's bit, under the Standard-Model paper's Hypothesis (S); the rest frame of the nonrelativistic limit is the laboratory's own and is not sourced by anything in the series; and the imaginary unit, Hestenes' spin plane, is the rest frame read through the law, one datum with the frame and not two, so it is not imported (Lemma \claimref{one-relation.one-datum-not-two-imaginary-unit}). Two uniqueness statements are proved outright by exact computation: among covariant constant-coefficient first-order operators acting by left multiplication the vector derivative is unique up to an invertible constant factor, and the Dirac current is the unique conserved constant sesquilinear current up to scale. Given that the law is first order, which is the one dynamical import, its form on even fields is forced by its square (Lemma \claimref{one-relation.form-law-forced-square}), and given the law the arrow of time and the frequency sign are one bit and not two, at $\Cl(1,3)$ level (Corollary \claimref{one-relation.arrow-frequency-are-one-bit-level}). The third constant is placed beside the other two: $c$ is the conversion constant between the charts, invisible in the Witt chart, which contains rapidity only, and fixed in the metric chart, one number by Witt's extension theorem and a conformal invariant, and the three constants together close the unit system with exponent determinant $-2$ (Lemma \claimref{one-relation.third-constant-conversion-constant-between-charts}). Born's rule is located rather than derived: the conserved density is that unique current, indifference forces equal weights on flag-degenerate components, and the residual postulate is isolated and named (that weights exist and add, a fragment smaller than Born but not zero), with the envariance literature credited as the argument's origin. Measurement is recording, collapse is converted into a vote whose premises are stated with their costs and whose stance is registered, and the character of experience closes as three theorems about record chains (recording structures, chains of committed records) under a supervenience premise: singleness, flow, and the dissolution of the branch question, with the hard problem declared the framework's final limit.

__notes__.note.one-relation.setting-laboratory-slo: The synthesis does not by itself reach the laboratory. Nonrelativistic quantum mechanics postulates three things the framework must either source or concede: a preferred time split, an imaginary unit, and a mass term. Of these the section sources one outright (the mass, at the level its Fact holds), sources half of the first (the time orientation, under the Standard-Model paper's Hypothesis (S)), declares the other half of the first, the rest frame, unsourced, and proves that the second was not a separate postulate at all: given the law, the imaginary unit is the rest frame read through it (Lemma \claimref{one-relation.one-datum-not-two-imaginary-unit}). It begins with the statement that is proved outright, and returns after the descent to the three lemmas that sharpen it.
__notes__.note.one-relation.point-contact-what-has: It would be a serious overstatement to say the framework derives quantum mechanics here, and this paper does not say it. What the section “The laboratory: the slow shadow” does is point at structures the series fixed for other reasons for the laboratory theory's three postulates, of which one is sourced, the mass (the condensate, at the level of the families paper's reading), one is half sourced, the time split (its orientation the flag, identified with the arrow under Hypothesis (S); its frame not sourced), and the third was not a postulate, the complex structure being the rest frame read through the law (Lemma \claimref{one-relation.one-datum-not-two-imaginary-unit}); and add four exact statements of its own, that the first-order operator acting on the left is unique, that the form of the law on even fields is forced by its square given first order, that the imaginary unit and the frame are one datum, and that the arrow and the frequency are one bit. The dynamics of the nonrelativistic descent from Dirac to Schr\"odinger is the textbook one, imported, and first-orderness is the one dynamical import. What remains genuinely postulated in the laboratory is the measure, and the section “Born, measurement, and the vote” isolates exactly how much of it the framework does not remove: a fragment smaller than Born's rule and not zero.
__notes__.note.one-relation.setting-spacetime-mani:
\textbf{The connection in words.} Gravity enters when the same construction is made at every point. The relation holds everywhere, so every point has its own light rays, its own bivector $\sigma$, and its own mode. That raises a question the relation cannot answer on its own: given the mode here, which mode over there is the same one? The connection answers it by carrying $\sigma$ from one point to the next along a path, keeping it as unchanged as the geometry allows, and this is what clause (3) means by the dynamics of the vacua. The answer can depend on the path. Carry $\sigma$ from here to there by one route and back by another, and it need not come home as the $\sigma$ you started with; it comes back tilted. That tilt is curvature, and the tilt is gravity (a figure of the original).

Two things should not be confused with this. The sign choice, which of the two rays is the creation operator, is not what tilts: a yes-or-no choice carried round a loop comes back either the same or flipped, and in a connected orientable spacetime it comes back the same. What tilts is the plane the choice was made on. And the fact that $g_{ab}$ takes different values at different points is not by itself curvature either: flat space can be written in coordinates where $g_{ab}$ varies and the light cones lean over, and nothing tilts on return. Curvature is what happens round the loop, not what the components look like at a point. Nothing here says why the geometry tilts things the way it does: the relation is satisfied by any metric, and what picks one is the field equation, which the geometry paper supplies \cite[Thm.~4.5]{ButlerT6} and this one does not. Gravity is not something added to the modes; it is the fact that the modes at different points cannot all be made the same mode, and the one bivector $\sigma$ is at once the label that says which state is occupied, the boost in its plane, and the thing that comes back tilted.
__notes__.note.one-relation.two-residues-named-so-: First, \emph{state selection}: Proposition \claimref{one-relation.two-presentations} identifies the kinematic algebra, and the physical state remains the flagged remainder of the thermality theorem; a selected state incompatible with the incidence-line structure of Proposition \claimref{one-relation.spacetime-manifold-vacuum-lines}, or one requiring more than the two real or three complex modes that the single ascent the conformal completion licenses, to $\Cl(2,4)$, supplies (Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-pure-spinors-incidence-chart}, Proposition \claimref{one-relation.two-capacities-three-consequences}), would break the vacuum-line reading. Second, \emph{the laboratory problem}: whether ordinary nonrelativistic quantum mechanics is recoverable as excitation dynamics above a vacuum chosen on a regular point's incidence line, with the Hamiltonian descending from the boost clock (the boost generator of the horizon pair, the singularity paper's clock) in the appropriate limit, is settled by no numbered result here; Proposition \claimref{one-relation.spacetime-manifold-vacuum-lines}(4) claims ubiquity only. the section “The laboratory: the slow shadow”-the section “The character of experience” carry that computation out at the levels they declare, and the claim is quantum mechanics everywhere, not only at interfaces. What the laboratory leaves as its remainder, after the sharpening of Lemmas \claimref{one-relation.form-law-forced-square} to \claimref{one-relation.one-datum-not-two-imaginary-unit}, is not the form of the law, which is forced, but why the evolution parameter is the frame's time and which frame: the frame cannot be sourced from the law, since the frozen point is $SO(1,4)$-invariant and any theorem selecting a $\gamma_{0}$ would break that; it is state data or observer data, and sourcing it is thermal time plus state selection, the geometric modular action the capstone carries as the open problem together with successor (2) here, and it is named and not opened. A third item, at programme level: if the earliest correlations are sourced by the descent, the primordial spectrum is the shape-shadow of a fibre state projected through the freezing, a computation whose output would confront the measured spectral index and would be a further registered stance; it is named in the successors and assigned to the capstone \cite{ButlerT17}.

__notes__.note.one-relation.setting-machine-verifi:
Every computational identity asserted in this paper at its own proof level has been verified in exact arithmetic by the script \texttt{verify\_T16.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT16}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py}: exact rationals, Gaussian rationals, the blade arithmetic for the frame computations, and exact linear algebra over the Gaussian rationals for the kernel computations. No floating point is used anywhere; one hundred and forty-six checks, all passing, in five parts, three of which have a second part. Every reference to the script in a proof above names a check in this list.

\emph{Part A: the two presentations.} The orthogonal relations of $\Cl(1,1)$ and, on the real null pair built from the same generators, the CAR of one mode; in $\Cl(1,3)_{\C}$ the real pair on the boost plane and the complex pair on the anisotropic kernel, all CAR relations exact, the change of basis of rank four over the Gaussian rationals, and the definiteness of the kernel ($Q(ae_{2} + be_{3}) = -(a^{2} + b^{2})$ on rational instances), which is why the real capacity is one and the complex two; in $\Cl(2,4)_{\C}$ two real pairs and one complex pair, all nine relation sets exact, and the kernel's definiteness again (real capacity two, complex three); and, for the paragraph in words after Proposition \claimref{one-relation.two-presentations}, the two occupation projectors $n_{-}n_{+} = \tfrac12(1+\sigma)$ and $n_{+}n_{-} = \tfrac12(1-\sigma)$ summing to one, the eigen-relations $\sigma n_{\pm} = \mp n_{\pm}$, and the three sign reversals of $(e_{0}, e_{1})$, of which the two single reversals swap the projectors and the double one fixes them.

\emph{Part B: capacity and overlap.} Arithmetic, recorded rather than tested, with one exception named: both capacities rise by exactly one under a $(1,1)$ ascent on the grid $p, q \leq 8$; the two capacity tables for the series' signatures ($1,1,2,3$ real and $1,2,3,4$ complex on $(1,1)$, $(1,3)$, $(2,4)$, $(3,5)$); the agreement locus $r_{\R} = r_{\C}$, proved in Proposition \claimref{one-relation.two-capacities-three-consequences} to be $|p - q| \leq 1$, illustrated on the grid by a biconditional check that could fail; and the two identities of Proposition \claimref{one-relation.overlap-table-sorted}(i).

\emph{Part C: the manifold of vacuum lines.} The null basis $n_{0}, n_{\infty}$ with $\ip{n_{0}}{n_{\infty}} = 1$; on six rational points with $Q(x)$ of every sign, $Q(X(x)) = 0$ computed from the inner product, $X(x)^{2} = 0$ in the algebra, $X(x) \neq 0$, and $Q(X) = Q(x)(1+2c) \neq 0$ for every other slot coefficient; the Fock model of $\Cl(2,4)_{\C}$ on $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$ built from wedge and contraction with all thirty-six anticommutators of the six ambient generators verified; for each point, $c(X(x))$ nilpotent with kernel of dimension four on the module and two on each chirality half; on each incidence line, two independent twistors and their sum each with a three-dimensional annihilator, pairwise distinct, each containing $X(x)$; across the fifteen pairs of points, distinct lines that meet exactly when the points are null-separated, and $\ip{X(x)}{X(y)} = -\tfrac12 Q(x-y)$ on every pair.

\emph{Part D: the laboratory.} The kernel of the covariance conditions for six rational rotors on the $64$-dimensional space of constant-coefficient first-order operators is two-dimensional and equals the span of $\gamma^{\mu}$ and $\gamma^{\mu}I$ (Lemma \claimref{one-relation.vector-derivative-covariant-first-order-operator}), with $I$ anticommuting with all four generators, $\gamma^{\mu}(a+bI) = (a-bI)\gamma^{\mu}$ on instances, $I^{2} = -1$ and $(a+bI)(a-bI) = a^{2} + b^{2}$ on instances; the boost plane squares to $+1$ and the spin plane to $-1$, the latter commuting with $\gamma_{0}$, and a rational rest-space rotation carries it to a distinct plane squaring to $-1$ and commuting with $\gamma_{0}$; the three algebraic facts of the Klein-Gordon square and $\{\gamma^{\mu}, \gamma^{\nu}\} = 2\eta^{\mu\nu}$ on all sixteen pairs; and the Pauli identity on nine rational vector pairs in $\Cl(3,0)$.

__notes__.note.one-relation.setting-two-presentati: \textbf{The relation in words.} Multiply two directions in either order, add the results, and what comes back is a number rather than a direction: that is the whole of $\{e_{a}, e_{b}\} = 2g_{ab}\mathbf{1}$. Taken on one direction with itself it says that a displacement squared is its own interval, which along a timelike direction is what a clock carried there reads. The same relation decides which directions have zero interval, because $g$ is what says so, and in the plane spanned by the time direction and any one spatial direction there are two such: the opposite light rays $n_{\pm} = \tfrac12(e_{0} \pm e_{1})$, for which the relation gives $n_{\pm}^{2} = 0$ and $\{n_{+}, n_{-}\} = 1$, the real null pair of the proof above. Those are the relations of a fermionic ladder pair, so $n_{+}^{2} = 0$ is at once the statement that a light ray has no length and the statement that no state holds two identical fermions. The two rays are not yet a creation operator and an annihilation operator, because nothing in the relation says which is which. Both are future directed, so a time orientation does not separate them; what does is the orientation of the plane they span, the sign of the bivector $\sigma = e_{0}e_{1}$, since $n_{-}n_{+} = \tfrac12(1 + \sigma)$ and $n_{+}n_{-} = \tfrac12(1 - \sigma)$ are the two occupation projectors and choosing the sign of $\sigma$ is choosing which of them counts as occupied. Reversing $e_{0}$ alone, or $e_{1}$ alone, swaps the roles; reversing both leaves them fixed. This is the sense in which the flag of Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-flag-arrow-superselection} is a $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ orientation and not a frame vector, and $\sigma$ is the boost generator whose rotor flow rescales the pair in Lemma \claimref{one-relation.third-constant-conversion-constant-between-charts}(iii) and which the singularity paper reads as its clock \cite{ButlerT5}. Once the sign is chosen the plane carries the kinematics of one fermionic mode: a two-state system with exclusion built in, and nothing more than that. Dynamics, a Hamiltonian, and the complex structure the usual Fock space needs are not in the relation and are not claimed here; over $\R$ the plane's algebra is $\Cl(1,1) \cong \Mat(2, \R)$, the real form of the one-mode CAR. The script checks the two projector identities, $\sigma n_{\pm} = \mp n_{\pm}$, and the three sign reversals.

__notes__.note.one-relation.two-presentations-diff: Proposition \claimref{one-relation.two-presentations} says that an orthogonal basis and a Witt basis generate the same algebra; this holds over every ring containing $\tfrac12$, and over the integers it fails. In $\Cl(1,1)$ let $e_{+}, e_{-}$ be orthonormal with $Q(e_{+}) = 1$, $Q(e_{-}) = -1$, and $a = \tfrac12(e_{+} + e_{-})$, $a' = \tfrac12(e_{+} - e_{-})$, so $a^{2} = a'^{2} = 0$ and $aa' + a'a = 1$. The integer span $\Lambda_{W}$ of the products of $a, a'$ is $\Z \oplus \Z a \oplus \Z a' \oplus \Z aa'$, and with $a, a', aa', a'a$ as the matrix units $E_{12}, E_{21}, E_{11}, E_{22}$ it is $\Mat_{2}(\Z)$, the integer form of Proposition \claimref{std-algebra.cl11-matrix}, with the integral idempotents $aa'$ and $a'a$. The integer span $\Lambda_{O}$ of the products of $e_{+}, e_{-}$ is $\Z \oplus \Z e_{+} \oplus \Z e_{-} \oplus \Z e_{+}e_{-}$, the matrices $\begin{psmallmatrix} \alpha & \beta \\ \gamma & \delta \end{psmallmatrix}$ with $\alpha \equiv \delta$ and $\beta \equiv \gamma \bmod 2$, a subring of index $4$ with $2\Lambda_{W} \subset \Lambda_{O}$, so $\Lambda_{O}[\tfrac12] = \Lambda_{W}[\tfrac12]$. Writing $x = \alpha + \beta e_{+} + \gamma e_{-} + \delta e_{+}e_{-}$, $x^{2} = (\alpha^{2} + \beta^{2} - \gamma^{2} + \delta^{2}) + 2\alpha(\beta e_{+} + \gamma e_{-} + \delta e_{+}e_{-})$, so every idempotent other than $0, 1$ has scalar part $\tfrac12$, and $\Lambda_{O}$, whose elements have integer scalar parts, has no idempotent other than $0$ and $1$; the idempotents $\tfrac12(1 \pm e_{+})$ of the orthogonal reading need $\tfrac12$. On the vector lattices the two presentations agree over $\Z[\tfrac12]$; over $\Z$ the null lattice $\Z a + \Z a'$, with $Q(xa + ya') = xy$ and the polar form $Q(u + v) - Q(u) - Q(v)$, is the even unimodular lattice $\mathrm{II}_{1,1}$ (the hyperbolic quadratic module, nonsingular), while the orthonormal lattice $\Z e_{+} + \Z e_{-}$, of index $2$ in it, is unimodular only for the half-polar form $B$, the odd lattice $\mathrm{I}_{1,1}$, and as a quadratic module it is singular at $2$ (polar determinant $-4$). So the metric chart and the CAR chart of the one relation are one object over the rationals and two different orders over the integers, and only the CAR chart contains the matrix units.
__notes__.note.pairing.abstract: The singularity paper places the pairing terms, the generators that change a Witt decomposition and so create entanglement from a vacuum, in the tangent of the vacuum orbit, and records two things it does not do: it compares two Witt decompositions without deriving them, and supplies no generator in that tangent. This note states both as claims with kill conditions fixed before computation, on the laboratory paper's pre-ascent Dirac fibre, two modes at a point, not the boundary-mode line. For the vacuum given by a null direction $\ell$ and a chirality bit, the stabiliser in $\so(1,3)$ is the parabolic algebra of $\ell$, and the functional $\pv(B) = \ip{B\cdot\ell}{m}$ that cuts it out is, on the Fock module, the pair-creation amplitude $-\bra{12}B\ket{0}$. The connection therefore has a pairing part, the transverse derivative of the null direction: the Newman-Penrose coefficients $\kappa, \tau, \sigma, \rho$. What is proved is the dictionary and the exact Schwarzschild classes; the identifications are imports, and the whole stands without the transport principle. In Schwarzschild, with $\ell$ the outgoing radial direction, only $\rho$ survives: zero along the $t$- and $r$-lines, zero on the horizon in a regular frame, opposite in sign on the two sides. Holonomy moves the vacuum only for loops with an $n \wedge \mb$ component, $\ell$ being a repeated principal null direction. The mismatch angle is not reached: the two frames share a vacuum, the selected transport has zero class, and no holonomy carries a mode weight. Nothing here pairs the ladders at two points.
__notes__.note.pairing.setting-setting-what-import:
The singularity paper reads entanglement as a mismatch of Witt decompositions and locates the generators that can produce it \cite[Prop.~13.4]{ButlerT5}: on the Fock space of $\nu$ modes the bivectors of $\so(2\nu)$ split into hops and pair annihilations, which stabilise the vacuum ray, and pair creations, which span the tangent of its orbit. The same paper then records, in one remark, the two things it does not do \cite[Rem.~13.5]{ButlerT5}: the framework compares two Witt decompositions and does not derive them, and the derivation of the one pairing angle its chain uses, the angle of its regularity premise, lies outside its reach. Its locality premise (L$_E$) \cite[Prem.~7.30]{ButlerT5} excludes pairing terms on the ground that the completion supplies none.

This note asks where, in the framework's own data, a pairing generator would have to come from, and answers: in the connection. The laboratory paper says in words that the connection carries the vacuum's bivector from point to point and returns it tilted \cite[Prop.~4.1(3) and the paragraph following it]{ButlerT16}. Stated exactly, the tilt has a stabiliser part and a pairing part, and the pairing part is the set of Newman-Penrose spin coefficients that measure how the null direction fails to be parallel. The note computes it, in the series' own conventions and in exact arithmetic, and then applies the kill conditions of the section “The two claims, and the kill conditions fixed before computation” to the two claims.

Three things are said on this page because the rest depends on them. First, the space. The singularity paper's premise governs the Fock space of its boundary modes, one ladder pair attached to each point of the exceptional set $E$ \cite[Prem.~7.30, Fact~5.9]{ButlerT5}, on which a pairing $v^{*}_{x}v^{*}_{y}$ is cross-point by construction and a single point carries no pairing at all. The fibre of this note is a different space: the pre-ascent Dirac spinor at an exterior point, read as two fermionic modes, the complex capacity two of the laboratory paper \cite[Prop.~3.2(1)]{ButlerT16}. What is found here is found on that fibre, and the section “What this does to the two claims” says what it does and does not imply for the premise. Second, the risk. The positive claim's kill conditions could not have fired (the section “What this does to the two claims”); the registration fixed the computation and its conventions in advance, and the note's content is a dictionary between the series' objects and known ones, not a derivation that might have failed. Third, the vocabulary, for a reader of general relativity and geometric algebra who has not read the series: the \emph{ascent} is the adjunction of a hyperbolic plane $(1,1)$ that the transport principle forces where division fails \cite[Thm.~4.13]{ButlerT1}, the \emph{completion} is its result, the \emph{exceptional set} $E$ is the locus where it happens \cite[Thm.~8.12]{ButlerT4}, the \emph{descent} is the one-way map back \cite[Thm.~7.3]{ButlerT5}, the \emph{flag bit} is the orientation choosing which half of a null pair creates \cite[Def.~2.10]{ButlerT14}, and the two-ledger words \emph{transport-essential}, \emph{convenient} and \emph{absent} grade a result by whether the $(1,1)$ increment does irreplaceable work in it, some work, or none \cite{ButlerT17}.

Notation follows the series. $\Cl(1,3)$ has $e_0^2 = 1$ and $e_i^2 = -1$; $\ip{a}{b} = \tfrac12(ab + ba)$ is the scalar product of vectors, extended bilinearly (not sesquilinearly) to $\C^4$; a bivector $B$ acts on vectors by $B\cdot v = \tfrac12[B, v]$, which is the $\so(1,3)$ action. The null tetrad is
\[
\ell = e_0 + e_1, \qquad n = e_0 - e_1, \qquad m = e_2 + i e_3, \qquad \mb = e_2 - i e_3,
\]
with $\ip{\ell}{n} = 2$, $\ip{m}{\mb} = -2$ and all other pairings zero. The framework's vacuum at a point is the maximal isotropic subspace $W = \operatorname{span}\{\ell, m\}$ of $\C^4$: $\ell$ is the radial null direction of the descent, the ladder vector of the singularity paper's Step 3 up to the flag bit \cite[Sec.~4, Lem.~4.1]{ButlerT5}, and the sign of $i$ in $m$ is the chirality bit. The Fock module is that of two modes with annihilators $a_1 = c(\ell)/2$, $a_2 = c(m)/2$ and creators $a_1^{\dagger} = c(n)/2$, $a_2^{\dagger} = -c(\mb)/2$, so that $e_0 = a_1 + a_1^{\dagger}$, $e_1 = a_1 - a_1^{\dagger}$, $e_2 = a_2 - a_2^{\dagger}$, $e_3 = -i(a_2 + a_2^{\dagger})$; this is the two-mode reading of the Dirac spinor, the complex capacity two of the laboratory paper.

__notes__.note.rungs.compact-form: The ambient signature at rung two is $(4,6)$, whose spin group is the noncompact $\mathrm{Spin}(4,6)$; the group in Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(3) is the compact $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$. They are two real forms of one complex group sharing the module, and the compact one is the real form fixed by the $*$-structure of the tower (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}), under which the ladder pairs are mutually adjoint, $v_{j}^{*} = w_{j}$: that adjointness is the Hermitian structure of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}, and the Bogoliubov group preserving it is the compact one. The $*$-structure is defined once the tower's frames are fixed, as T3 fixes them, so "fixed by" means fixed given the frames, a choice of maximal compact subgroup made once for the whole series rather than a consequence of the relations alone. The pattern is already present one rung down, where the ambient real form is the conformal $SU(2,2) \cong \mathrm{Spin}(2,4)$ (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-spinor-identification-witt-data-line}) while the pair-mixing group is the unitary group $U(3)$ of $W$ for the same adjointness, inside the compact three-mode Bogoliubov group. A grand-unification group must be compact, and the tower supplies the compact form for the same reason it supplies $U(3)$.
__notes__.note.rungs.setting-machine-verification: Every computational identity asserted here is verified in exact arithmetic by the deposited script \cite{ButlerVerifyT12R}, \texttt{verify\_T12\_rungs.py}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py}: seventeen checks, all passing, no floating point (ranks are computed by \texttt{GA.py}'s elimination over exact rationals). The script builds the five-mode Fock representation explicitly, as thirty-two by thirty-two matrices over the Gaussian integers, and the four-mode one of a single rung, and computes on them rather than restating formulas. They are: the canonical anticommutation relations, the uniqueness of the vacuum and the spanning of the module by creation monomials (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}, Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(1)); the chirality operator $(-1)^{N}$ as the parity of $j + k$, anticommuting with every generator; the bigraded dimensions counted on the basis; the ten Majorana generators' Clifford relations and the linear independence of the forty-five bilinears; their closure under the commutator with the $\mathfrak{so}(10)$ bracket on all pairs, and their commuting with chirality (Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(3)); the exact dimensions $25$ and $13$ of the subalgebras commuting with the total and with the separate mode numbers, giving $45 - 13 = 32 = 12 + 20$ (Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(2), (3), Proposition \claimref{rungs.generators-outside-gauge-algebra}, the section “The fallback: (S) as a Tier C premise”(iv)); the selection of $3N_{\mathrm{rung}} - 2N_{\mathrm{pair}}$ as the trace-free element of the centre, with eigenvalue $3j - 2k$, and the eigenvalue $j - k$ of $K$'s generator, zero on the cells only (Proposition \claimref{rungs.r-s-are-one-hypothesis-two}, Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(3)); the $\su(2)$ and $\su(3)$ Casimirs on every sector and the weights of $\Lambda^{2}W$ (Proposition \claimref{rungs.transported-module-holds-tuple-one-vector}, Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}); the ranks $17$ and $16$ at $n = 3$ against $12$ and $12$ at $n = 2$ (Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(3)); the two volume identities of Lemma \claimref{rungs.mass-bracket-frozen-points-grip-slot} on rational instances and the partial trace of $\Psi \otimes \bar\Psi$ over the slot index on a Gaussian-rational instance; the rung operators of $\uu(2)$ on the one-constituent even sector as the ladder action (Proposition \claimref{rungs.ladder-group-rung-mixing-group-one}); a null momentum staying null in $\Cl(2,4)$ and $\Cl(3,5)$ with the rungs' null pairs in \texttt{GA.py}'s blade engine (Corollary \claimref{rungs.fact-null-momenta-invite-one-rung}); the nullity of all six pairwise bivectors of a four-twistor instance, and, on the four-mode space, the twisted ground generators generating $\mathrm{M}_{8}(\C)$ with the rung's $\{1, v, w, vw\}$ as commutant, $v, w$ anticommuting with chirality and the even part abelian (Proposition \claimref{rungs.two-twistor-bivector-null-invites-one}; What the script does not check: the Facts beyond the instances named, verified in their own papers' scripts; the real-form statement of Remark \claimref{note.rungs.compact-form}, which is representation theory imported through Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}; and Hypothesis (R), which is not a computation.

one-relation.character-experience-three-.formal:
Grant Premise \claimref{one-relation.supervenience-stated-so-it-can-be}. Three statements follow about what any such subject must be like.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Singleness.)} A record chain reads only its own records, by the superselection of Remark \claimref{note.one-relation.measurement-recording-open-remainder} under Premise \claimref{one-relation.recording-irreversible-stated-so-it-can}, so no self can find, remember, or feel a sibling branch: experience must present as a single history however many the branches.
\item \emph{(Flow.)} A record chain writes in one direction on the modular period and never unwrites (Premise \claimref{one-relation.recording-irreversible-stated-so-it-can}), so experience must present as passage; and the direction of the felt passage is the flag itself. The arrow one experiences is the orientation bit of Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-flag-arrow-superselection}, read from inside, under Hypothesis (S) as that Fact records.
\item \emph{(The question dissolves.)} ``Why am I in this branch'' presupposes a branch-transcendent self that could have been located elsewhere, and no such object exists in the record structure: the self is individuated by the very records that constitute the branch, so each branch's subject asks the question and each is correct that this one is theirs. The question does not go unanswered; it goes unasked by anything real. This is the self-location analysis standard in the Everett literature \cite{Saunders2010, Wallace2012}, arrived at here from the record chain rather than postulated alongside it.
\end{enumerate}
The consequence is that the felt strangeness of quantum mechanics, that experience seems single, flowing, and unique despite the branching, is not residual strangeness at all: it is exactly what the branching structure looks like from inside one record chain. What remains, and is hereby declared the framework's final limit, is the hard problem proper: why there is anything it is like to be a record chain at all. On this the framework asserts nothing and derives nothing, and observes only that the question is invariant across every branch, every tower, and every physical theory yet written; it is not a residue of this framework but of physics. Structural level, conditional on Premises \claimref{one-relation.supervenience-stated-so-it-can-be} and \claimref{one-relation.recording-irreversible-stated-so-it-can}; refutation condition: exhibit experiential access to a sibling branch, or a felt arrow decoupled from the recording direction, and the identification fails.
one-relation.character-experience-three-.technical:
Granting the supervenience premise (a self is a record chain) and the irreversible-recording premise, three structural statements follow. Singleness: a record chain reads only its own records, which are superselected from sibling branches, so experience presents as one history. Flow: records are written in one direction on the modular period and never unwritten, so experience presents as passage, and the felt direction is the flag's orientation bit read from inside, under Hypothesis (S). Dissolution: asking why I am in this branch presupposes a branch-transcendent self, which the record structure does not contain, so the question goes unasked by anything real.

What remains is declared the framework's final limit: the hard problem, why there is anything it is like to be a record chain, on which nothing is asserted or derived. The result is structural and conditional on both premises; it fails if experiential access to a sibling branch, or a felt arrow decoupled from the recording direction, is exhibited.
one-relation.character-experience-three-.lay: If a conscious self is nothing more than a chain of permanent records, and recording cannot be undone, then a self in a branching quantum world should feel exactly as we do. It sees one history, feels time passing in one direction (read as the framework's arrow, which also assumes that the slots of the conformal spinors behave like the pairs, Hypothesis (S)), and has no real question about why it is in this branch rather than another. The framework says nothing about why there is any experience at all, and calls that its final limit.

Levels pass: lay and one-liner now keep Hypothesis (S), an assumes edge, for the arrow clause.

proofs.main: Each clause is the imported structure read under the premise. (1) is Remark \claimref{note.one-relation.measurement-recording-open-remainder}'s inaccessibility applied to a subject constituted by records in one sector; the content is that the supervenience (\claimref{one-relation.supervenience-stated-so-it-can-be}) premise turns an operational statement about correlations into a statement about what a self can contain. (2) is the irreversibility of Premise \claimref{one-relation.recording-irreversible-stated-so-it-can} on the modular period of Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-single-mode-thermality-modular-period}, together with the flag identification of Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-flag-arrow-superselection}, under Hypothesis (S) (\claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}) as that Fact records: the writing direction is the flag's orientation, and under the premise the felt direction is the writing direction. (3) is the self-location argument: a subject individuated by a record chain has no counterpart in a sibling chain to be identified with, so the indexical question has no referent capable of being surprised by its answer. The proposition proves nothing about the hard problem and says so.

one-relation.dirac-current-conserved-den.formal: Let $\psi$ range over solutions of the Dirac equation $(i\gamma^{\mu}\partial_{\mu} - m)\psi = 0$ with $m > 0$, in a matrix representation with $\{\gamma^{\mu}, \gamma^{\nu}\} = 2\eta^{\mu\nu}$, $\gamma^{0}$ Hermitian and $\gamma^{k}$ anti-Hermitian, and let $\bar{\psi} = \psi^{\dagger}\gamma^{0}$. Among the constant sesquilinear currents $J^{\mu}_{\Gamma} = \bar{\psi}\,\Gamma^{\mu}\psi$, $\Gamma^{\mu} \in \Mat(4, \C)$ constant, those conserved on every solution ($\partial_{\mu}J^{\mu}_{\Gamma} = 0$) form the one-dimensional space spanned by $\Gamma^{\mu} = \gamma^{\mu}$. The density of that current, $J^{0} = \bar{\psi}\gamma^{0}\psi = \psi^{\dagger}\psi$, is a sum of squared moduli, positive and zero only on the zero state.
one-relation.dirac-current-conserved-den.technical:
For solutions of the Dirac equation $(i\gamma^{\mu}\partial_{\mu} - m)\psi = 0$ with $m > 0$, consider the constant sesquilinear currents $J^{\mu}_{\Gamma} = \bar{\psi}\Gamma^{\mu}\psi$. Those conserved on every solution form a one-dimensional space, spanned by $\Gamma^{\mu} = \gamma^{\mu}$. Its density $J^{0} = \psi^{\dagger}\psi$ is a sum of squared moduli, positive and vanishing only on the zero state.

Conservation on every solution reduces to the linear condition $(p - p')_{\mu}\bar{u}\Gamma^{\mu}v = 0$ over mass-shell plane waves; $\gamma^{\mu}$ satisfies it, and an exact finite sample of momenta already cuts the solution space down to one dimension.
one-relation.dirac-current-conserved-den.lay: The Dirac equation describes the electron relativistically. Among all the simple candidate currents one can build from its solutions, only one is conserved for every solution, the standard Dirac current. Its time component, the density, is always positive and is zero only when there is no wave at all.
one-relation.dirac-current-conserved-den.typing_note: No edges; the lemma is itself standard Dirac theory proved directly, and no imported standard Dirac-current claim exists in the store for a standard-route derivation.

proofs.main:
Every solution is a finite or continuous superposition of plane waves $u\,e^{-ip\cdot x}$ with $p$ on the mass shell $p^{2} = m^{2}$, either sign of $p^{0}$ allowed, and $u \in \ker(\slashed{p} - m)$, a two-dimensional space at each such $p$. For a finite superposition $\psi = \sum_{k} u_{k}e^{-ip_{k}\cdot x}$ one has $\partial_{\mu}J^{\mu}_{\Gamma} = i\sum_{k,l}(p_{k} - p_{l})_{\mu}\,\bar{u}_{k}\Gamma^{\mu}u_{l}\,e^{i(p_{k} - p_{l})\cdot x}$, the diagonal terms vanishing identically; for a two-term superposition the two cross terms carry the distinct nonzero exponents $\pm i(p_{1} - p_{2})\cdot x$, which are linearly independent functions, so conservation on every solution is equivalent to
\[
(p - p')_{\mu}\,\bar{u}\,\Gamma^{\mu}\,v = 0 \qquad \text{for all mass-shell } p, p',\ u \in \ker(\slashed{p} - m),\ v \in \ker(\slashed{p}' - m),
\]
a linear condition on the $64$ complex entries of $(\Gamma^{0}, \dots, \Gamma^{3})$. Lower bound: $\Gamma^{\mu} = \gamma^{\mu}$ satisfies it, since $\bar{u}\slashed{p} = m\bar{u}$ (take the adjoint of $\slashed{p}u = mu$ using $\gamma^{0}\gamma^{\mu\dagger}\gamma^{0} = \gamma^{\mu}$) and $\slashed{p}'v = mv$, so $\bar{u}(\slashed{p} - \slashed{p}')v = (m - m)\bar{u}v = 0$. Upper bound: the space of solutions for all $(p, p', u, v)$ is contained in the space of solutions for any finite sample, and the script takes $m = 5$, twelve rational mass-shell momenta including negative-energy ones (for instance $(13, 12, 0, 0)$, $(7, 2, 4, 2)$, $(13, \tfrac{36}{5}, \tfrac{48}{5}, 0)$, $(-9, -4, 6, 2)$), the exact two-dimensional kernels $\ker(\slashed{p} - m)$ at each, and all $528$ resulting conditions over the Gaussian rationals; the kernel of that system is one-dimensional and contains $\gamma^{\mu}$. The two bounds meet. Positivity: $\bar{\psi}\gamma^{0}\psi = \psi^{\dagger}(\gamma^{0})^{2}\psi = \psi^{\dagger}\psi$, a sum of squared moduli; the script confirms the anticommutation and Hermiticity relations of the representation and the density on exact instances. That this current is, in Hestenes' form, the geometric current $J = \psi\gamma_{0}\tilde{\psi}$ with the density its $\gamma_{0}$ component is the standard translation of the Dirac bilinears into the spacetime algebra, imported \cite{Hestenes1975}.

one-relation.form-law-forced-square.formal:
Let $C \in \Cl(1,3)$ be constant. Every solution of $
abla\psi = m\,\psi\,C$ satisfies the Klein-Gordon equation $
abla^{2}\psi = -m^{2}\psi$ if and only if $C^{2} = -1$; $C^{2} = +1$ gives $
abla^{2}\psi = +m^{2}\psi$, the tachyonic sign, and a non-scalar $C^{2}$ gives no scalar second-order equation at all. Hestenes' right factor $C = \gamma_{0}(I\sigma_{3})^{-1}$ has $C^{2} = -1$; $C = I\gamma_{0}$ has $C^{2} = +1$; $C = \gamma_{3} + I\gamma_{2}$ has a non-scalar square.
one-relation.form-law-forced-square.technical:
For a constant $C \in \Cl(1,3)$, applying the vector derivative twice to $
abla\psi = m\psi C$ gives $
abla^{2}\psi = m^{2}\psi C^{2}$, since $
abla$ acts on the left and $C$ on the right. So every solution is Klein-Gordon, $
abla^{2}\psi = -m^{2}\psi$, if and only if $C^{2} = -1$; $C^{2} = +1$ gives the tachyonic sign, and a non-scalar $C^{2}$ gives no scalar second-order equation.

Hestenes' factor $C = \gamma_{0}(I\sigma_{3})^{-1}$ squares to $-1$; $I\gamma_{0}$ squares to $+1$; $\gamma_{3} + I\gamma_{2}$ has a non-scalar square.
one-relation.form-law-forced-square.lay: A first-order wave equation of this type, applied twice, should give the familiar relativistic relation between energy, momentum and mass. Whether it does depends only on the square of one constant factor in the law. That square must be minus one; any other choice gives faster-than-light behaviour or no sensible equation at all.
one-relation.form-law-forced-square.typing_note: No edges; the proof is self-contained.

proofs.main:
Since $
abla$ acts on the left and $C$ is constant, $
abla(
abla\psi) = 
abla(m\psi C) = m(
abla\psi)C = m^{2}\psi C^{2}$, so $
abla^{2}\psi = m^{2}\psi C^{2}$, which is $-m^{2}\psi$ for every solution if $C^{2} = -1$. Conversely, the law has a solution invertible at the origin: for a field depending on $t$ alone, $
abla\psi = \gamma_{0}\partial_{t}\psi$ and the law reads $\partial_{t}\psi = m\gamma_{0}\psi C$, a linear ordinary differential equation with constant coefficients, whose solution with $\psi(0) = 1$ is invertible at $t = 0$; if every solution is Klein-Gordon then $\psi C^{2} = -\psi$ at the origin for this one, so $C^{2} = -1$. The same solution shows that $C^{2} = +1$ gives the tachyonic sign and a non-scalar $C^{2}$ no scalar equation. The script checks $I\sigma_{3} = \gamma_{2}\gamma_{1}$, $(I\sigma_{3})^{-1} = -I\sigma_{3}$, and the three squares stated.

one-relation.imported-cartans-purity-the.formal:
A Weyl spinor of $\mathrm{Spin}(2
u, \C)$ is \emph{pure} if it is the Fock vacuum of some maximal isotropic subspace, equivalently of some Witt decomposition of $\C^{2
u}$. Every Weyl spinor is pure for $2
u \leq 6$; in dimension $8$ purity is one quadratic condition, the $\mathrm{Spin}(8)$-invariant form on the half-spinor space, and in higher dimension it is more. The pure spinors form a single orbit, the spinor variety, of dimension $
u(
u - 1)/2$. For any antisymmetric $A$, the Thouless state $\exp(\sum_{i<j}A_{ij}a^{\dagger}_{i}a^{\dagger}_{j})|0angle$ is the vacuum of the Witt decomposition obtained from the standard one by the corresponding Bogoliubov rotation, and every vacuum with nonzero overlap with $|0angle$ is of this form. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Cartan1938, Chevalley1954} for purity and the spinor variety; \cite{Thouless1960} for the exponential form.
one-relation.imported-cartans-purity-the.technical:
A Weyl spinor of $\mathrm{Spin}(2
u, \C)$ is pure if it is the Fock vacuum of some maximal isotropic subspace. Every Weyl spinor is pure when $2
u \leq 6$; in dimension $8$ purity is one quadratic condition, and in higher dimension it is more. The pure spinors form a single orbit, the spinor variety, of dimension $
u(
u - 1)/2$.

For antisymmetric $A$, the Thouless state $\exp(\sum_{i<j}A_{ij}a^{\dagger}_{i}a^{\dagger}_{j})\ket{0}$ is the vacuum of the Bogoliubov-rotated Witt decomposition, and every vacuum with nonzero overlap with $\ket{0}$ has this form. Purity and the spinor variety are imported from Cartan and Chevalley, the exponential form from Thouless.
one-relation.imported-cartans-purity-the.lay: In a system of fermion modes, some states are the empty state, or vacuum, for some way of splitting the modes into creators and annihilators; these are called pure spinors. In small systems every state of fixed parity is of this kind, while in larger ones only special states are. These classical results also give an explicit formula for all such vacua that overlap a reference one.

one-relation.measure-indifference-borns-.formal: The unique conserved density among constant sesquilinear ones is the Dirac density of Lemma \claimref{one-relation.dirac-current-conserved-density}, the $\gamma_{0}$ component of the geometric current $J = \psi\gamma_{0}\tilde{\psi}$: positivity, conservation and uniqueness in that class are proved. The current is fixed up to scale; the \emph{density} is its component along a timelike $\gamma_{0}$, which is the laboratory's rest frame, declared unsourced in Proposition \claimref{one-relation.schr-odinger-slow-shadow}(3): the located Born density is frame-relative, and the paper says so here rather than leaving it implicit in the lemma. What remains of Born's rule is the identification of this density with occupation weight, and the framework closes part of the remaining gap with its founding principle, the indifference premise (Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-indifference-instrument}, a structural premise of the series and not a theorem): for a superposition of equal-norm, flag-degenerate components, any unequal weight assignment would instantiate a preference nothing caused, so indifference forces equality; rational weights follow by fine-graining into equal-norm constituents permuted by Witt rotations that are exact symmetries of the frozen vacuum; and continuity completes the squared-norm measure as the only assignment consistent with vacuum indifference. This is the envariance argument \cite{Zurek2005} transplanted into the framework's vocabulary, and it inherits that argument's standing critique: the fine-graining step presupposes that weights compose additively, which is a fragment of the probabilistic reading it derives. That presupposition is hereby isolated as the residual postulate, smaller than Born and not zero: \emph{that weights exist and add}. Structural-conditional level, with the refutation condition stated: exhibit a weight assignment respecting vacuum indifference that is not the squared norm, and the reduction fails.
one-relation.measure-indifference-borns-.technical:
The unique conserved density among constant sesquilinear ones is the Dirac density, the $\gamma_{0}$ component of the geometric current $J = \psi\gamma_{0}\tilde{\psi}$; it is positive, conserved and unique in that class, and frame-relative, since $\gamma_{0}$ is the laboratory's unsourced rest frame. Identifying it with occupation weight uses the indifference premise: equal-norm, flag-degenerate components related by exact vacuum symmetries must receive equal weight; fine-graining then gives rational weights and continuity the squared-norm measure.

This is the envariance argument in the framework's vocabulary and it inherits that argument's critique: fine-graining presupposes that weights exist and add, which is isolated as the residual postulate, smaller than Born's rule but not nothing. The level is structural and conditional; a weight assignment respecting vacuum indifference that is not the squared norm would refute the reduction.
one-relation.measure-indifference-borns-.lay: Born's rule says the chance of a quantum outcome is the squared size of its part of the wave. Here the relevant density is fixed as the unique conserved, positive one, measured in the laboratory's rest frame. Then the series' indifference premise, a declared starting point and not a theorem, that nothing may prefer one of several equivalent outcomes, forces equal chances for equal parts and builds up to the squared-size rule. One assumption remains, that chances exist and add up, and the paper names it as what is still postulated, so the result is conditional on both.
one-relation.measure-indifference-borns-.typing_note: Kept both edges; the slow-shadow proposition in context_refs is cited only for the unsourced frame and is not a premise; the envariance argument (Zurek) is the standard counterpart but is not in the store, so no standard-route derivation. Levels pass: the lay level now marks indifference as a premise rather than a theorem, keeps the frame-relativity of the density and says the result is conditional.

proofs.main: The current's positivity, conservation and uniqueness are Lemma \claimref{one-relation.dirac-current-conserved-density}. The indifference step is Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-indifference-instrument} applied to components related by an exact symmetry of the vacuum, which is precisely the instrument's licensed use (equating along orbits), and \emph{not} the illicit use audited in the families paper (equating inequivalent components). The script exhibits the licensed step in miniature: on $n = 2, 3, 4, 5$ equal-norm components the weight vectors invariant under all transpositions form a one-dimensional space, the uniform one, while under an intransitive subgroup (one transposition, or two disjoint ones, on four components) the invariant space has dimension three or two, one per orbit, and under the transitive Klein four-group it is again one-dimensional: equality is forced by transitivity on the components, which is what an exact orbit supplies; and on three rational instances the fine-graining of a two-component state into equal-amplitude constituents returns the squared norms on the branches. The fine-graining and continuity steps are the envariance argument's, imported with its critique. The isolation of the additivity fragment is the proposition's content and is stated, not proved.

one-relation.odd-square-roots-chiral-pha.formal: An odd element of $\Cl(1,3)$ is $C = v + Iw$ with $v, w$ vectors, and $C^{2} = Q(v) + Q(w) - 2I\,(v \wedge w)$. Hence $C^{2} = -1$ if and only if $v \wedge w = 0$ and $Q(v) + Q(w) = -1$, that is $C = (\cos t + \sin t\, I)\,u$ with $u$ a unit spacelike vector. Two freedoms act on this set. The representation freedom $\psi \mapsto \psi R$ for a constant rotor $R$ carries $C$ to $\tilde{R}CR$ and moves $u$ over the whole one-sheeted hyperboloid of unit spacelike vectors, on which $\mathrm{Spin}^{+}(1,3)$ is transitive. The chiral phase $\psi \mapsto \psi\exp(tI)$ carries $C$ to $C\exp(2tI)$, because $I$ anticommutes with odd elements, and so removes $t$; it is not a rotor, its reverse being itself and not its inverse, and it shifts the Takabayasi angle by the constant $2t$. Consequently, for the single free fermion with minimal electromagnetic coupling that this section treats, and in that scope only, every first-order covariant law $\nabla\psi = m\psi C$ on $\Cl^{+}(1,3)$ whose square is Klein-Gordon at mass $m$ is the Dirac-Hestenes equation up to a constant field redefinition, the parity of the fields forcing $C$ to be odd (a law with an even part of $C$ admits no even solution invertible anywhere); with Yukawa or weak couplings the chiral phase of a mass is physical and the redefinition is not free.
one-relation.odd-square-roots-chiral-pha.technical:
An odd element of $\Cl(1,3)$ is $C = v + Iw$ with $v, w$ vectors, and $C^{2} = Q(v) + Q(w) - 2I(v \wedge w)$. So $C^{2} = -1$ exactly when $C = (\cos t + \sin t\, I)u$ with $u$ a unit spacelike vector. Constant rotors $\psi \mapsto \psi R$ move $u$ over the whole hyperboloid of unit spacelike vectors, and the chiral phase $\psi \mapsto \psi\exp(tI)$ sends $C$ to $C\exp(2tI)$, removing $t$; it is not a rotor, and it shifts the Takabayasi angle by $2t$.

Since $\psi$ is even and $\nabla$ odd, an even part of $C$ would leave no even solution invertible anywhere, so $C$ is odd. Hence, for a single free fermion with minimal electromagnetic coupling only, every first-order covariant law $\nabla\psi = m\psi C$ on $\Cl^{+}(1,3)$ squaring to Klein-Gordon at mass $m$ is the Dirac-Hestenes equation up to a constant field redefinition. With Yukawa or weak couplings the chiral phase is physical and the redefinition is not free.
one-relation.odd-square-roots-chiral-pha.lay: An earlier result says the constant factor in the electron's law must square to minus one. This one lists every allowed factor and shows that, for a single free electron, they all give the same equation seen in a rotated frame or with a harmless constant phase. Once other interactions are included, that phase is no longer harmless.

one-relation.one-datum-not-two-imaginary.formal: Align the representative so that $C = Iu$. The complex structures the descent of step (4) needs are the constant even $J$ with $J^{2} = -1$ commuting with $C$, so that the plane-wave factor $\exp(-Jp \cdot x)$ passes through $C$. The commutant of $C$ in $\Cl^{+}(1,3)$ is four-dimensional, spanned by $1$ and the three bivectors of the $3$-space orthogonal to $u$ (for $u = \gamma_{3}$: $1, \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}, \gamma_{0}\gamma_{2}, \gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$); the pseudoscalar, though even and a square root of $-1$, anticommutes with $C$ and is excluded. On the commutant $J^{2} = -1$ iff the scalar part vanishes and the bivector part has unit timelike-signature norm, a two-sheeted hyperboloid. The map $J \mapsto \gamma_{0} := CJ$ is a bijection from that hyperboloid onto the unit timelike vectors orthogonal to $u$, with inverse $J = C^{-1}\gamma_{0}$. So, given the law, choosing the imaginary unit and choosing the rest frame are one choice, not two. The joint commutant of $(C, J)$ in $\Cl^{+}(1,3)$ is $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, whose rotors form the $U(1)$ of rotations in the spin plane, Hestenes' electromagnetic phase, which minimal coupling already uses. Any laboratory frame can be aligned: if the laboratory's $\gamma_{0}$ is not orthogonal to the representative's $u$, a rotor of the freedom of Lemma \claimref{one-relation.odd-square-roots-chiral-phase} realigns $u$, and that freedom is used up there, once, and is not to be counted again as the empty freedom of step (3).

That $CJ$ is a vector: $C = Iu$ with $u$ orthogonal to the plane of $J$, so $uJ = u \wedge J$ is a trivector, and $I$ times a trivector is a vector (\claimref{std-algebra.duality}); the sign computation, $CJ = \pm\gamma_{0}$ at $J = \gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$, is recorded by the script and is the choice of sheet. one-relation.overlap-table-sorted.formal: Three numerical agreements in this series are read as consequences of the one relation having two charts. They are not of one kind, and the proposition sorts them; none is an agreement of independent computations. \emph{(i) One count in two vocabularies.} The tower's one-qubit-per-rung ladder is read off the periodicity isomorphism $\Cl(p+1,q+1) \cong \Mat(2, \Cl(p,q))$, one matrix doubling per rung; the capacity increment of Proposition \claimref{one-relation.two-capacities-three-consequences}(2) is index arithmetic. The isomorphism is the tower paper's structure theorem (Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-completion-ladder}); its dimension shadow $2^{p+q+2} = 4 \cdot 2^{p+q}$ and the increment are identities that cannot fail, and the step that reads a matrix doubling as one mode is exactly the identification of Proposition \claimref{one-relation.two-presentations}; the content is that the metric reading's doubling and the Witt reading's mode are one count. \emph{(ii) An identification.} The pair count $(n+2)/2 = 3$ at spacetime dimension $n = 4$, under which the Standard-Model paper selects the strong force and four dimensions on its two declared conditionalities, is proved there to be the maximal isotropic dimension of the complexified ascended space, by the same argument this paper gives for the complex capacity \cite[Lem.~2.12]{ButlerT12}; its equality with $r_{\C}(2,4)$ of Proposition \claimref{one-relation.two-capacities-three-consequences}(3) is therefore an identification and not an agreement: the pairs of a conformal spinor (the twistor's pairs) are the fermionic modes of the complex reading, so the Standard-Model paper's count is a quantum capacity, and what is new here is only the extension to arbitrary signature with the attainment construction. \emph{(iii) A reading.} The thermality theorem (Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-single-mode-thermality-modular-period}) is single-mode, its mode being the ladder pair of the ascent, a mode adjoined by the rung and not the boost pair of $(1,3)$; Proposition \claimref{one-relation.two-capacities-three-consequences}(2) says a rung adjoins exactly one mode in either count. That the theorem is single-mode \emph{because} one rung was ascended is the structural explanation this paper offers, and it is a reading of the two results together, not a computation; the theorem installs one mode per point of the singular boundary (Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-single-mode-thermality-modular-period}, \cite[Thm.~8.12]{ButlerT4}), so the reading concerns each marginal and not a capacity ceiling. At observation level, each presentation also carries a constant, and the three constants are at three levels: $\hbar$ as the ordering shift of the Witt presentation, the half-per-mode shift proved in the correspondence paper T9 \cite[Prop.~5.6]{ButlerT9}; $G$ as the compositeness scale of the metric presentation, the dimension-two irrelevance the dark-energy paper T10 reads at structural level from its acoustic no-go, the no-go itself conditional on the singularity paper's premise (Q), within an acoustic programme that paper closes at the mixed level of its inputs, the sphere step conditional on the indifference premise \cite[Prop.~5.2, Rem.~5.3, Assembly~5.5]{ButlerT10}; and $c$ as the datum of the transition between the two charts, invisible in the Witt chart, which contains rapidity and no other quantity, and fixed in the metric chart, which contains time and length separately (Lemma \claimref{one-relation.third-constant-conversion-constant-between-charts}, proved). The third is placed by a different mechanism from the first two, and it is a conformal invariant, surviving every conformal step the first two do not. This is an identification of \emph{where} the constants enter, not a derivation of their values, and it remains the synthesis's weakest point, flagged as such; what can be said in its favour is this: $c$ has no value to derive, its number being a unit convention, and in the Planck system all three are, so a placement can be nothing more than this.
one-relation.overlap-table-sorted.technical:
Three numerical agreements in the series are sorted, and none is an agreement of independent computations. (i) One count in two vocabularies: the tower's one qubit per rung, read from $\Cl(p+1,q+1) \cong \Mat(2, \Cl(p,q))$, and the capacity increment per rung are one count, via the identification of the metric and Witt presentations. (ii) An identification: the Standard-Model pair count $(n+2)/2 = 3$ at $n = 4$ is the complex capacity $r_{\C}(2,4)$, so that count is a quantum capacity. (iii) A reading, not a computation: the thermality theorem is single-mode because one rung adjoins exactly one mode.

The three constants are placed at three levels: $\hbar$ as the ordering shift of the Witt presentation, $G$ as the compositeness scale of the metric presentation (at the conditional level of its sources), and $c$ as the datum of the transition between the two charts, which is proved. This locates where the constants enter and derives no values; it is flagged as the synthesis's weakest point.
one-relation.overlap-table-sorted.lay: Several numbers in this series of papers match up, and it would be tempting to count each match as independent confirmation. This result sorts them: one is the same count written two ways, one is a direct identification, and one is an interpretation. It also says, at observation level, where Planck's constant, Newton's constant and the speed of light enter the picture, without claiming to compute their values; the placement of Newton's constant rests on earlier premises (the singularity paper's premise (Q) and the indifference premise), and the paper flags this placement as the synthesis's weakest point.

one-relation.record-chain-votes-measurem.formal:
The question left standing by Remark \claimref{note.one-relation.measurement-recording-open-remainder} has the exact shape of a question this series has already answered at cosmic scale, and the transposition is recorded with its premises stated with their costs. At the origin the descent faced multiple superselected sectors, and the conclusion was threefold, each clause with its own source: selecting one sector would be an uncaused preference the indifference premise forbids (Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-indifference-instrument}); superselection renders the sectors mutually \emph{dark} rather than mutually exclusive (Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-flag-arrow-superselection}); hence all flaggable sectors are occupied, weighted by the one measure, and ``why is ours the visible one'' is indexical, not dynamical, which is the dark-matter paper's premise form of indifference, scoped there to the reversal orbit and extended here to all flag sectors (Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-indifference-instrument}). After a measurement, by Remark \claimref{note.one-relation.measurement-recording-open-remainder} under Premise \claimref{one-relation.recording-irreversible-stated-so-it-can}, the laboratory presents the identical structure in miniature: flag sectors dynamically disconnected by irreversible recording. The same premises force the same conclusion: all branches occupied, weighted by the measure of Proposition \claimref{one-relation.measure-indifference-borns-rule-located}, mutually dark, with the experienced single outcome the view from inside one record chain.

A second, independent argument closes from the other side. The framework's freedom is a \emph{fixed and finite count}: two numbers and one bit, counted across the series (Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-flag-arrow-superselection}, \cite[Prop.~7.6]{ButlerT12}, \cite[Prop.~5.1, Prop.~5.2]{ButlerT14}), the two numbers on the dark-matter paper's declared stance that the framework inherits its asymmetry rather than generating it, and the bit under the three premises of the corrected orientation argument (CPT covariance, an antilinear conjugation whose action clause covers the gauge couplings; Hypothesis (S); and the flag as a datum of each solution, \claimref{dark-matter.premise-flag-as-datum}); the exhaustiveness of a trichotomy, the third premise of that paper's version, is not used. Dynamical collapse produces a new uncaused bit per event, unboundedly many, outside that count; on the stance and under the premises, a mechanism that uses freedom the framework does not possess is not an open alternative within it.

Two gaps are named so the vote can be refuted. First, the \emph{disanalogy}: tower superselection is exact and algebraic, while laboratory decoherence is emergent, irreversibility on the modular period rather than a theorem of charge, so the transposition holds in the recording limit and is structural-conditional there. Second, the \emph{residue}: indexicality dissolves ``why this branch'' as a dynamical question without answering it as an experiential one, and this paper says so. The vote is nonetheless testable, and a conditional stance is registered: no objective-collapse signature at any sensitivity, no spontaneous-localisation noise and no gravitationally induced collapse \cite{GRW1986, Penrose1996}, since any confirmed collapse mechanism would be the uncaused selector this framework forbids. Continued null results are consistent with this stance; one confirmed signature refutes the stance, the counting argument, and the vote together.
one-relation.record-chain-votes-measurem.technical:
After a measurement, under the irreversible-recording premise, the laboratory has the structure the series met at cosmic scale: flag sectors dynamically disconnected. The same premises, indifference forbidding an uncaused selection and superselection making the sectors mutually dark, give the same conclusion: all branches are occupied, weighted by the squared-norm measure, and the single experienced outcome is the view from inside one record chain.

A second argument: the framework's freedom is a fixed finite count, two numbers and one bit (on the inherited-asymmetry stance and under the premises behind the bit, including Hypothesis (S)), while dynamical collapse needs a fresh uncaused bit per event. Two gaps are named: laboratory decoherence is emergent rather than exact, so the transposition is structural-conditional in the recording limit, and indexicality dissolves the question of why this branch dynamically without answering it experientially. The stance is testable: one confirmed objective-collapse signature refutes it.
one-relation.record-chain-votes-measurem.lay: When a measurement is made, the framework, granting its stated premises (that an unexplained preference is forbidden, that recording is irreversible, and, behind its count of free numbers, Hypothesis (S) on the slots' statistics), says every possible outcome happens, each in its own branch that cannot see the others, rather than one outcome being picked by a physical collapse. It argues this in two ways: picking one outcome would be an unexplained preference, and collapse would need an endless supply of new random choices the framework does not have. The parallel with the cosmic case holds only in the limit of ideal recording, since laboratory decoherence is approximate, and the account leaves open why this branch is the one experienced. This is a testable, conditional bet: any confirmed sign of real wavefunction collapse would refute it.

one-relation.schr-odinger-slow-shadow.formal:
The laboratory equation is the algebra's own first-order operator viewed from inside a rest frame. The chain, in four steps, with each input's provenance declared.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The operator; proved.)} The first-order operator is the vector derivative $\nabla = \gamma^{\mu}\partial_{\mu}$, unique up to an invertible constant factor among covariant constant-coefficient first-order operators acting by left multiplication (Lemma \claimref{one-relation.vector-derivative-covariant-first-order-operator}): native to the Clifford presentation, no postulate.
\item \emph{(The mass comes from the condensate; sourced. The form of the law; forced, given first order.)} The equation of motion is the Dirac-Hestenes equation $\nabla\psi\, I\sigma_{3} = m\,\psi\gamma_{0}$, Hestenes' real form of the Dirac equation \cite{Hestenes1967, Hestenes1975}. What is imported is one sentence, that the law is first order, Dirac's factorisation of the mass shell; the form is then forced: a first-order covariant law $\nabla\psi = m\psi C$ with constant right factor squares to Klein-Gordon at mass $m$ iff $C^{2} = -1$ (Lemma \claimref{one-relation.form-law-forced-square}), and every odd such $C$ is the Dirac-Hestenes factor up to the representation freedom and a constant chiral phase, the latter a field redefinition for the single free minimally coupled fermion treated here (Lemma \claimref{one-relation.odd-square-roots-chiral-phase}). Its mass parameter is the mass of Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-condensate-derived-content}: applying $\nabla$ twice gives $\nabla^{2}\psi = -m^{2}\psi$, so every component of a solution is a Klein-Gordon field $(\Box + m^{2})\psi = 0$ of the same $m$, which is the quantity the mass-weight dictionary quantifies as the composite's grip on the frozen point. That $\Lambda \neq 0$ makes condensation unavoidable is the families paper's observation-level reading (Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-condensate-derived-content}); the mass term is therefore sourced at the level of that reading and of the dictionary, and no higher.
\item \emph{(The imaginary unit is the rest frame read through the law; one datum, proved. The time orientation is the flag; sourced under Hypothesis (S). The rest frame is not sourced.)} In Hestenes' form the unit imaginary is the bivector $I\sigma_{3} = \gamma_{2}\gamma_{1}$, a spacelike plane in the rest space of $\gamma_{0}$, which squares to $-1$ and commutes with $\gamma_{0}$; it is not the boost plane, which squares to $+1$. Given the law, the complex structures the descent can use are the even $J$ with $J^{2} = -1$ commuting with the right factor, and $J \mapsto \gamma_{0} = CJ$ is a bijection between them and the unit timelike vectors orthogonal to the law's spacelike datum: choosing the imaginary unit and choosing the rest frame are one choice (Lemma \claimref{one-relation.one-datum-not-two-imaginary-unit}), so the imaginary unit is not a third postulate to be imported. The pair $(\gamma_{0}, I\sigma_{3})$ on the right of the equation is fixed only up to the representation freedom $\psi \mapsto \psi R$ for constant rotors $R$, which Hestenes identifies as physically empty and which Lemma \claimref{one-relation.one-datum-not-two-imaginary-unit} uses up once, to align the law's datum with the laboratory; the residual freedom is the $U(1)$ of the spin plane, the electromagnetic phase. What the series fixes is therefore not the plane and not the frame vector $\gamma_{0}$ but a single bit: the particle-antiparticle orientation, which is the sign convention separating positive-frequency from negative-frequency solutions, and which Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-flag-arrow-superselection} identifies with the arrow of time and argues to be initial data under three premises, one of them the open Hypothesis (S); the orientation is sourced under (S) and not otherwise. The \emph{rest frame} of the nonrelativistic limit, the choice of which timelike $\gamma_{0}$ the laboratory is at rest in, is the laboratory's own, and nothing in this series selects it: the frozen point is de Sitter-invariant and singles out no time direction, and since the law fixes only $C$ of the triangle $(C, J, \gamma_{0})$, any theorem selecting $\gamma_{0}$ would break that invariance; the frame is state data or observer data, never law data. Given the law, the frequency sign and the direction of the frame's time are one bit, not two (Corollary \claimref{one-relation.arrow-frequency-are-one-bit-level}).
\item \emph{(The nonrelativistic descent; imported.)} For excitations near the mass gap, factor the rest phase $\psi = \varphi\exp(-I\sigma_{3}mt)$ in the laboratory's frame and expand in $|\mathbf{p}|/m$: at first order the Pauli equation, with the gyromagnetic ratio $g = 2$ automatic, an inherited check passed; suppressing the spin sector, the Schr\"odinger equation in a potential, the potential entering as the electrostatic component of the one gauge connection by minimal coupling, which is, on the Standard-Model paper's observation-level reading of its forced connection, a holonomy constraint rather than an ansatz (Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-condensate-derived-content}). The algebraic input of the $g = 2$ step is the Pauli identity $\mathbf{a}\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b} + I_{3}\,\mathbf{a}\times\mathbf{b}$ in the rest space, whose antisymmetric part is what doubles the spin coupling relative to the orbital one.
\end{enumerate}
Structural level: the nonrelativistic descent in step (4) is the standard one and is imported as such, and first-orderness is the one dynamical import; the framework's contribution is that of the three postulated inputs, the mass is fixed by the condensate at its Fact's level, the orientation half of the time split is fixed by the flag under Hypothesis (S) with the arrow-equals-frequency identification proved at $\Cl(1,3)$ level, the imaginary unit is carried by the rest frame and is not a separate input, and the rest frame is declared unsourced: of three postulates, one is sourced, one is half sourced, and the third was not a postulate. Nonrelativistic quantum mechanics is the Dirac shadow of the frozen phase, seen slowly, from a frame the laboratory supplies.

The laboratory equation is the algebra's first-order operator viewed from a rest frame, in four steps. (1) The vector derivative $
abla = \gamma^{\mu}\partial_{\mu}$ is the unique covariant first-order operator up to an invertible constant. (2) Importing only that the law is first order, its form is forced to the Dirac-Hestenes equation $
abla\psi\, I\sigma_{3} = m\,\psi\gamma_{0}$ for the single free minimally coupled fermion, and its mass is the condensate's mass at the level of the imported reading, since $
abla^{2}\psi = -m^{2}\psi$. (3) The imaginary unit $I\sigma_{3}$ is the rest frame read through the law, the frequency sign and time direction are one bit sourced by the flag under Hypothesis (S), and the rest frame itself is unsourced. (4) The standard nonrelativistic descent, imported, gives the Pauli equation with $g = 2$ and then the Schr"odinger equation in a potential.

Of the three postulated inputs (mass, time split, imaginary unit), one is sourced, one is half sourced, and the third was not a separate postulate. The level is structural, with first-orderness the one dynamical import.
